summary: Georgetown County, SC tower built by the SC Forestry Commission in 1937 beside US 17; register calls it presently inactive (2017); no later condition report found.

facts.status_note: Register (registered 2017) calls it presently inactive; no later report on whether it still stands

access.note: No access information on the register or the Forest Lookouts page

visit.trail_note: Register places it along US 17 south of Georgetown; no visit route or climbing information found

events.note: Register 'Built' field gives 1937; built by the South Carolina Forestry Commission
Civilian Conservation Corps repainted the living quarters at the tower site, 1938-39 (year given is the first year of the work)

evidence.supports: built by the SC Forestry Commission in 1937 as a 100' Aermotor tower located along US 17 south of Georgetown
evidence.quote: Built by the South Carolina Forestry Commission in 1937, this 100' Aermotor tower is located along US 17 south of Georgetown, South Carolina.

evidence.supports: register calls the tower presently inactive

evidence.quote: January 2014 photo - courtesy of Gary Weber

evidence.supports: CCC enrollees repainted the living quarters at the tower site in 1938 and 1939
evidence.quote: 1938-39: Civilian Conservation Corps enrollees repainted the living quarters at the tower site.

evidence.supports: source of the 1938-39 work is a state forestry report
evidence.quote: Report of the State Commission of Forestry, year ended 6/30/1939

notes_for_editor: Only two sources, and neither gives a current condition. The Former Fire Lookout Sites register has no entry for this tower (firetower.org/lookouts/us/sc/winyah-bay-lookout/ returns 404). Two searches turned up no news or photo report after 2017. 'Standing' is the brief's record; the register's 'presently inactive' is the only support, and status_note says so. The 1938 modified year covers 1938-39 work. The Forest Lookouts page cites a 1939 state report that was not read directly. Recommend a recent photo or local source before publication.
